name: MacMoney
tagline: A native macOS replacement for Microsoft Money.
summary: MacMoney is a native Mac app for people who still keep their finances in Microsoft Money Plus Sunset Edition. It imports a Money file with its whole history, keeps the way Money works (registers, flags, bills and deposits, payee reports, forecasting) and adds what Money never had: safe bank-download imports, item-level purchases, what-if scenarios and Schedule C tracking for a home business.
description: Microsoft Money was discontinued years ago and only runs on Windows. MacMoney reads the .mny file directly, read-only, and brings in accounts, categories, payees, transactions, splits, transfers, flags and recurring bills. Importing again is safe, so Money and MacMoney can run side by side until the switch is final.

From there it is a full personal-finance app. Bank and card downloads go in without ever adding a transaction twice. Registers reconcile against statements. A forecast projects balances from bills and deposits, and what-if scenarios show what a decision would do before it is made. One or more sole-proprietor businesses can be tracked through their own accounts or tagged inside personal ones, producing a draft Schedule C.
Everything stays on the Mac. The app makes no network connections, the data is a standard SQLite file, and backups are verified and can be encrypted.
role: Solo project: design, development and documentation
techStack: Java (Jackcess) for the Money file converter

Re-import as often as you like: Money's records update in place and everything added in MacMoney is kept

A backup is taken before every import

Payments already entered by hand are matched instead of duplicated

Flags with a note and an action date

Itemize any charge by hand, from any store

Notes, web links and receipt files (referenced where they are, never copied)

points: Find across every account, open or closed
Per-payee trend chart, totals by year and by category, every transaction, CSV export
Select several payees at once; save selections and filters as presets
Back and forward navigation between reports

features.summary: Recurring items that keep their day of the month.
points: Weekly, every other week, twice a month, monthly, quarterly, yearly and more
Enter, skip, or pre-load everything due into the right registers
Transfer bills post to both accounts
Optional auto-pay flag on entered items

features.summary: A balance projection that never double counts, plus named scenarios laid over it.
points: Today's balance + entries made ahead + bills not yet entered
3 to 36 months or a custom range, for one account or all bank accounts
Hover the chart to see what moves the balance each day
Scenarios: one-time or recurring amounts, changed or stopped bills, drawn against the baseline with the difference shown

technicalHighlights.title: Reading a format with no specification
technicalHighlights.detail: A Money file is an encrypted Jet database with an undocumented schema. A small bundled Java converter (built on Jackcess) opens a copy read-only and writes JSON; the app decodes that and merges it. The schema notes worked out along the way are published in the repository.

technicalHighlights.title: Re-import that is always safe
technicalHighlights.detail: Every record from Money carries its Money id, and the importer writes only Money-owned fields. App-owned fields (business tags, tax lines, notes, presets) live separately, so importing the same file a hundred times changes nothing and loses nothing.

technicalHighlights.title: Bank imports that never duplicate
technicalHighlights.detail: Each bank row gets a fingerprint (the bank's reference, or date + amount + normalized description, with an occurrence number so two identical same-day charges stay two). Fingerprints are remembered even after the transaction is edited or deleted. Rows that match something already in the register within a week are linked rather than added.

technicalHighlights.title: Exact money, stable dates
technicalHighlights.detail: Amounts are integer cents everywhere; there is no floating point where money is added up. Dates are calendar days stored at noon UTC, so a transaction never changes day when the time zone does.

technicalHighlights.title: Fast with decades of history
technicalHighlights.detail: Views never walk the SwiftData relationship graph. A ledger index keeps plain value rows, built once at launch (about 0.6 s for 8,000 entries) and patched from save notifications (about 40 ms). Large lists use a custom NSTableView wrapper with fixed row heights instead of SwiftUI's Table, which froze for seconds on 7,500 rows; it shows them in about 5 ms.

technicalHighlights.title: Backups you can rely on
technicalHighlights.detail: Backups use SQLite's online backup API, so they are consistent while the app is running, and each one is integrity-checked after it is written. Encrypted backups use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM in authenticated 1 MB chunks. Restores are staged and applied before the store is opened, after a safety copy of the current data. New record types are added so that an older backup still opens: a test builds a data file from before the newest model existed, restores it over newer data, and checks both.

technicalHighlights.title: Private by construction
technicalHighlights.detail: The app makes no network connections. Receipts are referenced by bookmark, not copied. The data is a standard SQLite file in Application Support that the owner can open with any tool.

technicalHighlights.title: Ready for iCloud sync
technicalHighlights.detail: All 19 models follow CloudKit's rules from the start (defaults or optionals on every attribute, optional relationships, no unique constraints), with identity carried by a uuid.

technicalHighlights.title: Screenshots without real data
technicalHighlights.detail: A built-in demo mode generates five years of an invented household from a seeded generator. The app photographs its own window screen by screen, and every picture is read back with OCR and rejected if the developer's name or home folder appears in it. The pictures on this page were made that way.

sampleData.note: Every screenshot shows invented sample data. No real person, account or amount appears.
sampleData.household: A two-income household over five years: a salaried job, a freelance design business (Juniper Lane Studio) with its own accounts, and a small print shop (Tidepool Prints) run through the personal accounts. Mortgage, car loan, two credit cards, savings and an index fund.

roadmap: Purchases on Schedule C: a business purchases report by line, for the accountant
Purchase rules: vendor and department defaults so new imports arrive already tagged
Card and bank follow-ups: link card payments to the checking payments that paid them, payee cleanup rules, a business review queue
Smaller purchase items: hide a whole order, attachments on any register transaction
